# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

# Evaluating agents

## pass@k vs pass^k
pass@k: any of k runs succeeds. pass^k: all k succeed. Reliability is what deployment needs.

## Proxy vs direct measures
A quiz score is a proxy. Retention a week later is closer to the thing itself.

Built a web-search agent with two tools. Latency was the main issue.

# Agent environments

## What an environment is
State, observations, actions, dynamics. The reward is a separate claim about what matters.

## Partial observability (POMDP)
When the agent cannot see the full state it must maintain a belief and sometimes act to gather information. Measurement can be an action with a cost.

## Attention as a hidden variable
Learners do not read everything shown to them. Attention gates learning and drains with fatigue.

args.text:
Here’s a concrete version of your build writeup you can adapt:

What I built: I built a study assistant that helps a student read course materials, answer messages, and manage study tasks on their computer.

Environment definition: 
- State: the visible course files, notes, calendar, messages, and the student’s current attention/motivation.
- Observations: what the assistant can read from the computer UI and messages.
- Actions: open/read sections, send messages, append notes, schedule study blocks, and quiz the student.
- Dynamics: student attention changes over time, messages and quizzes affect what the student learns, and some important state (like attention) is hidden.

Why that fits Week 3: this is a partially observable environment because the assistant can’t directly see the student’s full internal state. Attention acts like a hidden variable, and choosing when to quiz or nudge the student is like gathering information at a cost.

Evaluation: I measured reliability with pass^k, not pass@k. pass^k means all k runs succeed, which is the stricter metric for dependable deployment. I reported pass^k on at least 3 seeds.

If you want, I can also help you turn this into a polished paragraph instead of bullets.
